title: Adaptive Helpfulness-Harmlessness Alignment with Preference Vectors
abstract: arXiv:2504.20106v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Ensuring that large language models (LLMs) are both helpful and harmless is a critical challenge, as overly strict constraints can lead to excessive refusals, while permissive models risk generating harmful content. Existing approaches, such as reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) and direct preference optimization (DPO), attempt to balance these trade-offs but suffer from performance conflicts, limited controllability, and poor extendability. To address these issues, we propose Preference Vector, a novel framework inspired by task arithmetic. Instead of optimizing multiple preferences within a single objective, we train separate models on individual preferences, extract behavior shifts as preference vectors, and dynamically merge them at test time. translated_title: 基于偏好向量的自适应有用性-无害性对齐
translated_abstract: 确保大语言模型（LLM）既有用又无害是一项关键挑战，因为过于严格的约束会导致过度拒绝，而过于宽松的模型则存在生成有害内容的风险。现有方法，如基于人类反馈的强化学习（RLHF）和直接偏好优化（DPO），试图平衡这些权衡，但存在性能冲突、可控性有限和可扩展性差的问题。为了解决这些问题，我们提出了偏好向量，这是一种受任务算术启发的新型框架。与在单一目标中优化多个偏好不同，我们在各个偏好上分别训练模型，将行为变化提取为偏好向量，并在测试时动态合并它们。这种模块化方法实现了细粒度的、用户可控的偏好调整，并支持在不重新训练的情况下无缝集成新偏好。实验……
tldr: 该论文提出“偏好向量”框架，通过为每个偏好单独训练模型并提取偏好向量，在推理时动态合并，实现了大语言模型有用性与无害性之间细粒度、用户可控的自适应对齐，且无需重新训练即可集成新偏好。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the Preference Vector framework, which trains separate models for individual preferences, extracts behavior shifts as preference vectors, and dynamically merges them at test time, enabling fine-grained, user-controllable helpfulness-harmlessness alignment for LLMs with seamless integration of new preferences without retraining.
